mission: Torin makes the best possible case for the technique while the Codex material explains what the wound actually is and why it will not heal on its own.
why_now: The Codex's heresy is now on the table. With the technique named at R04b and the wound's mechanism specified here, the chain that links Veraine's procedure to Veranthos is legible in outline for the first time. Sera's warning in the corridor lands because Ben has just understood -- in his body -- the scale of what Torin's reading is trying to justify.
conflict: Torin's reading of the Codex is intellectually beautiful. If Ankhural's heresy is right, the technique is correction rather than violation. The argument is seductive in proportion to how well it fits the evidence -- and the evidence, just revealed by R04c, is worse than Ben had let himself understand. In the same archive material, Veraine's clinical annotation about pressure, drainage, and scar geometry lands without ideology, introducing her working mind before her person arrives. Ben's susceptibility is the warning, not his speech.
turning_point: Ben catches the motion of his own head nodding to Torin's last sentence. He stops it. Sera sees him catch it, and pulls him aside.
opening_hook: Torin holds the Codex fragment and doesn't flinch. Everyone else did
closing_hook: Sera, very quietly to Ben, names the argument's lineage without naming Gavran — she has heard this one before, from a man she followed into a war. She doesn't say the name. She doesn't need to
emotional_trajectory: Absorbing the wound's mechanism -> intellectual engagement with Torin's reading -> seductive logic -> Sera's cold water

stakes.personal: Ben nearly seduced by Torin's interpretation — a warning about his own susceptibility, sharpened by the fact that he has just understood what the wound actually costs
stakes.interpersonal: Sera trusting Ben enough to name Gavran in the same breath as Torin, even without the name
stakes.external: Torin's relationship with the technique is deepening; the wound's architecture is legible as a sustained human cost

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — common area, then private corridor exchange
sensory_details: The Codex's records resolving into wound-mechanics — the anchor system as an engineered architecture, not a containment field; Torin's Force presence when he holds the Codex — the heaviness lifting into something lighter and more dangerous; Sera's jaw tight; Kael's expression saying without saying that both positions prove his point; Ben's understanding of the mechanism landing in his stomach a beat before it lands in his head
canon_elements_needed: Force wound theory with Nihilus and Malachor V precedent
Anchor system architecture — Force-sensitives used as structural load-bearing in a sealed wound
Jedi Lords era containment engineering; twelve-anchor configuration rationale
action_beats: Torin lifts the Codex fragment and holds it steady while the others watch for a reaction that doesn't come

The fragment's records resolve — the wound's mechanism named, the anchor system specified, twelve living Force-sensitives as sustained structural rebar. R04c lands. Ben registers the mechanism through his body before his mind processes it
Torin's reading of the same material lands as correction-not-violation — coherent, beautiful, dangerous
Sera steps close enough to place her hand flat on the table between Torin and the artifact
Sera pulls Ben into the corridor and speaks with her back to the common area door
notes: The danger here is seduction. Ben should almost agree, and Sera's warning should land because she can hear the old pattern returning.
